sections.title: The Capstone Model
learningObjectives: Understand why L4B's final assessment takes a capstone project format rather than a standard written/practical test
Recognize how this differs from assessment structures earlier in the curriculum
sections.content: Earlier levels pair a written test with a practical assessment, apart from Level 1, which is a knowledge check. L4B's capstone is different by design, borrowed from engineering degree practice: a real, substantial project demonstrating integrated competency across everything the Advanced Programming track has covered, evaluated by peer review rather than a standard pass/fail quiz. Competency is demonstrated through actual work, not exam answers.

keyTerms.note: A substantial project that shows you can combine everything in the track, assessed on the work itself.

sections.title: What the Capstone Involves
learningObjectives: Understand the general scope of a capstone project
Recognize how it draws on the full L4B module sequence
sections.content: The capstone project synthesizes the preceding L4B modules - CNC machine tending integration, PLC integration, complex payload configuration (lift and rotate), and fleet optimization - into a single substantial project brief, rather than testing each skill in isolation. The specific project brief is being developed with DiFacto SME input, reflecting real integration scenarios the role actually encounters.

keyTerms.note: A person with deep specialized knowledge, consulted or co-authoring content for highly technical modules.

sections.title: Project Documentation
learningObjectives: Understand what documentation a capstone submission requires
Recognize why documentation quality is itself part of the assessment
sections.content: A capstone submission isn't just a working solution - it includes documentation of the design decisions made, the integration approach taken, and the testing performed to validate it. This mirrors what's actually expected of an Advanced Programmer in the field: a working system that nobody else can understand or maintain isn't considered complete work.

sections.title: Peer Review Process
learningObjectives: Understand the general structure of peer review for this capstone
Recognize the value of peer review beyond pass/fail determination
sections.content: Peer review means the capstone is evaluated by others who've completed or are completing the same track, not solely by an instructor - reflecting how real engineering work gets reviewed in practice. Specific panel composition and review process will be confirmed with DiFacto as the pilot cohort structure is finalized. Beyond determining pass/fail, peer review exposes candidates to different approaches other participants took to similar problems.

keyTerms.note: Evaluation of your work by others who have completed or are completing the same track.

sections.title: Evaluation Criteria
learningObjectives: Understand the general categories a capstone is evaluated against
Recognize that evaluation covers design, build, test, and documentation together
sections.content: Capstone evaluation uses a structured rubric covering design quality, build/implementation, testing rigor, and documentation - not a single pass/fail criterion on whether the system technically works. A technically functional solution with poor documentation or inadequate testing does not meet the bar this capstone sets.

keyTerms.note: A structured set of criteria used to score work consistently, here covering design, build, testing, and documentation.

sections.title: Completing Advanced Programming Certification
learningObjectives: Understand what DiFacto Certified Advanced IMR Programmer status represents
Recognize the path forward into L5
sections.content: Successfully completing the capstone, evaluated by panel review, completes the requirements for DiFacto Certified Advanced IMR Programmer status - the highest technical certification level before L5 (Master Instructor). This status reflects genuine integration competency demonstrated through real work, consistent with how the capstone model was designed from the outset.

questions.question: How does L4B's final assessment differ from earlier levels?
options: A longer written exam taken in a single sitting replaces the practical
A peer-reviewed capstone project replaces the standard test
An observed live delivery replaces the written test, as at Level 5
questions.feedback: Correct. The capstone model is deliberately different, borrowed from engineering degree practice.

questions.question: What does the capstone project synthesize?
options: The L4A modules on safety PLC design, enterprise architecture, and multi-plant rollout planning
Only the module the candidate found hardest in the track
CNC integration, PLC integration, complex payloads, and fleet optimization in one brief
questions.feedback: Correct. The capstone draws together the full L4B module sequence into one integrated project.

questions.question: Is documentation part of what's being assessed, or just the working solution?
options: Yes, documentation quality is assessed alongside the working solution
No, only whether the integrated system works is scored by the reviewers
Only when reviewers cannot get the solution to run on their own
questions.feedback: Correct. A working system without adequate documentation is not considered complete work.

questions.question: Who evaluates the capstone project?
options: A single instructor, with no input from other candidates on the track
Peers who have completed or are completing the same track
An automated test suite that scores the working system on its own
questions.feedback: Correct. Peer review reflects how real engineering work is typically reviewed in practice.

questions.question: What does completing the capstone achieve?
options: Automatic entry into L5 without any further requirement
Certification as a Systems Engineer through the L4A route
It completes the Advanced IMR Programmer certification requirements
questions.feedback: Correct. Successful capstone completion confers DiFacto Certified Advanced IMR Programmer status.
